dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: An indexed outer run package for dimensions m,n,t,b1,b,b2,p,q,r. Its constructor D015 packages matrices, perturbation parameters, dimension and positivity proofs, and one inner entry run for each output index.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The universally quantified run supplies every datum and implicit hypothesis used by the bound.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projection of the run's real matrix A, indexed by Fin m × Fin n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supplies A in the exact matrix-product entry and the absolute-product sum.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projection of the run's real matrix B, indexed by Fin n × Fin t.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supplies B in the exact matrix-product entry and the absolute-product sum.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: For output indices i,j, this is the computed value stored by the corresponding inner entry run.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the approximate quantity compared with the exact matrix-product entry.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef005
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projection of the outer real parameter uBar.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It enters γ_n(uBar), the inner error bounds, and the stability condition n·uBar<1.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef006
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projection of the outer real parameter uFma.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Together with uBar and uOut, it determines the piecewise effective parameter used in γ_q.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef007
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projection of the outer real parameter uLow.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It bounds both input perturbations and appears explicitly as 2uLow+uLow² and (1+uLow)².

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef008
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projection of the outer real parameter uOut.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It contributes to the piecewise effective parameter used in γ_q.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef009
dependency_coverage.meaning: The componentwise absolute-product sum Σ_{k∈Fin n}|A(i,k)|·|B(k,j)|.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: This nonnegative sum scales the entire error coefficient on the right-hand side.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef010
dependency_coverage.meaning: For real parameters v,u and naturals q,n, it is γ_q(v)+γ_n(u)+γ_q(v)γ_n(u), where γ_s(w)=s·w/(1-s·w).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With v equal to the effective piecewise parameter and u=uBar, it forms the second error contribution.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef011
dependency_coverage.meaning: The piecewise value e: e=uOut if uFma<uOut; otherwise e=0 if uFma≤uBar; otherwise e=uFma.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The bound uses γ_q(e), and every inner run bounds its δ errors by e and assumes q·e<1.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef012
dependency_coverage.meaning: The exact matrix-product entry Σ_{k∈Fin n}A(i,k)B(k,j).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: This is subtracted from the computed entry inside the absolute error.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef013
dependency_coverage.meaning: The computed value of an inner run, defined as its state at natural index q.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It identifies each outer computed entry with the terminal state s_q of the modeled recurrence.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef014
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projection assigning an inner run of dimensions n,b,q to every output pair (i,j).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It provides the recurrence whose terminal state is the computed entry at i,j.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef015
dependency_coverage.meaning: Constructor for an outer run. dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: These constructor requirements are the complete outer hypotheses under which the stated pointwise bound applies.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef016
dependency_coverage.meaning: The rational function γ_n(u)=n·u/(1-n·u), using the natural number n cast to a real.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef017
dependency_coverage.meaning: The stability predicate n·u<1.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef018

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef026

binders: run is an outer run package indexed by those nine natural numbers.
i is an arbitrary element of Fin m and j is an arbitrary element of Fin t.
hypotheses: Existence of run entails m,n,t,b1,b,b2,p,q,r>0 and the exact dimension factorizations m=p·b1, n=q·b, and t=r·b2.
The run contains arbitrary real matrices A:Fin m×Fin n→Real and B:Fin n×Fin t→Real.
It contains input-error arrays eA and eB satisfying |eA(i,k)|≤uLow and |eB(k,j)|≤uLow for every valid index.
The real parameters uLow,uHigh,uBar,uFma,uOut are nonnegative; uHigh≤uLow; uFma∈{uLow,uHigh}; uOut∈{uLow,uHigh}; and uBar≤uFma.
Define e=uOut when uFma<uOut; if that test is false and uFma≤uBar, define e=0; otherwise define e=uFma. The stability assumptions are q·e<1 and n·uBar<1.

For each output pair (i,j), the run contains an inner entry run with the same uBar,uFma,uOut. Writing φ(k,l)=l+b·k under n=q·b, its block data satisfy x(k,l)=A(i,φ(k,l))(1+eA(i,φ(k,l))) and y(k,l)=B(φ(k,l),j)(1+eB(φ(k,l),j)).

For each inner run there are an order tag, a state s:Nat→Real, carry errors c_k, term errors τ_{k,l}, and errors δ_k such that s_0=0 and, for every k=0,…,q-1, s_{k+1}=[s_k(1+c_k)+Σ_{l=0}^{b-1}x(k,l)y(k,l)(1+τ_{k,l})](1+δ_k).
The local bounds are |δ_k|≤e, |c_k|≤γ_b(uBar), and |τ_{k,l}|≤γ_b(uBar) when k=0 and ≤γ_{b+1}(uBar) when k>0.
For every k,l there are n inner-path errors ε_{k,l,r} with |ε_{k,l,r}|≤uBar and ∏_{r=0}^{n-1}(1+ε_{k,l,r})=(1+τ_{k,l})∏_{h=k+1}^{q-1}(1+c_h).

If the inner order tag equals the distinguished constructor D029, then additionally |c_k|≤γ_1(uBar), and there are q+b-1 right-to-left path errors η_{k,l,r}, each bounded by uBar, whose one-plus product equals (1+τ_{k,l})∏_{h=k+1}^{q-1}(1+c_h).
mathematical_definitions: γ_s(u)=s·u/(1−s·u), with s interpreted as a real.
e=uOut if uFma<uOut; e=0 if uFma≥uOut and uFma≤uBar; and e=uFma if uFma≥uOut and uFma>uBar.
The exact product entry is C(i,j)=Σ_{k=0}^{n-1}A(i,k)B(k,j).
The computed entry is the corresponding inner terminal state s_q.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every outer run satisfying the encoded positive-dimension, block-factorization, parameter, multiplicative-input-perturbation, stability, recurrence, local-error, and path-product conditions, every computed output entry differs from the corresponding exact real matrix-product entry by at most the stated scalar coefficient times the componentwise absolute-product sum for that entry.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: Although the dimensions are universally quantified over all naturals, an outer run can be constructed only when every listed dimension and block parameter is positive and the three factorization equalities hold. For other choices the theorem is vacuous because no run exists.

The theorem quantifies over already constructed run packages; it does not assert that a run or any of its recurrence and path-error witnesses exists for arbitrary matrices and parameters. Inconsistency of those packaged hypotheses would make the statement vacuous.
The conclusion is a pointwise scalar entry bound. It does not state a matrix-norm, vector-norm, componentwise relative-error, or backward-stability result.
A and B are otherwise unrestricted real matrices. The input perturbations are encoded multiplicatively as A(1+eA) and B(1+eB), with absolute bounds on eA and eB.

All arithmetic in the proposition and its error model is exact real arithmetic. No finite representability, rounding mode, overflow, underflow, exceptional values, or concrete implementation behavior is encoded beyond the supplied recurrence and error identities.

The conditions q·e<1 and n·uBar<1 make the two γ denominators occurring in the final bound positive. The positivity and n=q·b conditions also control the γ denominators used by the active inner bounds.
The inequality uHigh≤uLow is formal despite the parameter names; no interpretation of either parameter as a particular precision is encoded.
The parameters b1,b2,p,r affect admissibility through m=p·b1 and t=r·b2 but do not otherwise occur in the final coefficient or inner recurrence.
Only the distinguished order value D029 receives the extra sharper carry and right-to-left path requirements; the formal proposition supplies no comparable extra conditions for other order tags.
There are no existential witnesses in the conclusion: state functions and all error/path arrays are fields already carried by run.
ambiguities: The dossier does not provide human-level semantic names for the constructors of LocalDef028. Formally, D029 is exactly the constructor whose equality activates the additional conditions, but its intended algorithmic order cannot be identified from the supplied types alone.
